LEADER, JUDGMENT CALL ON RELATION: Lisa Lutoff-Perlo was a named executive officer for 2020 to 2023 but not for 2024 (pay-versus-performance footnote), and she is not in the 2025 proxy's directors-and-executive-officers ownership table, so status is no-reported-stake with values null. The schema has no value for the CEO of a subsidiary brand (Celebrity Cruises); 'former-ceo' is used and should be read as former brand CEO, not former CEO of Royal Caribbean Group. HOLDERS: the three largest 5% holders are listed; the proxy gives 13G/A filing dates (Capital Research Global Investors February 13, 2025; Vanguard July 10, 2024; AWILHELMSEN AS February 12, 2025, plus a Form 4 of November 21, 2024), not the dates the holdings refer to, so asOf is null. Director Arne Alexander Wilhelmsen's 18,174,326 shares (6.69%) include the 18,167,507 AWILHELMSEN AS shares (he disclaims beneficial ownership of them), so he is not listed separately. No Pritzker entity appears in the 2025 proxy's 5% table, so none is recorded. BlackRock (6.0%) and Capital World Investors (5.1%) are the other 5% holders. DIVIDENDS: cash paid was $107 million; dividends declared in 2024 were $255 million ($0.95 per share, equity statement); the cash-paid figure is used. BUYBACKS: none; the equity statement shows $12 million of treasury stock purchases, not described as repurchases (the 10-K says there were no repurchases of common stock in 2024). GEOGRAPHY: the company's table is by cruise itinerary region, not customer location; 'North America' includes the United States, Canada, Mexico and the Caribbean. 'Other revenues' ($788 million: cancellation fees, insurance, tours, port fees, services to affiliates) is not assigned to a region and is shown as its own row. Separately, the 10-K says 75% of 2024 passenger ticket revenues came from guests sourced in the United States.

footprint.notes: Workforce from the FY2024 10-K (Dec 31, 2024): ~106,000 employees, of which 4,250 shoreside staff are U.S.-based and everyone else (4,850 shoreside, 95,150 shipboard, 1,750 at private destinations) is international, recorded as one region. Country shares are of the shoreside workforce (U.S. 47%, Philippines 34%, Mexico 6%, U.K. 4%). The 10-K also says the shipboard crew comes mostly from the Philippines (33%), Indonesia (17%) and India (15%); that is crew nationality, not where people work, so it is kept out of the rows. The 10-K describes two operating private destinations (CocoCay, owned; Labadee, leased); planned ones not open in FY2024 (Royal Beach Club Paradise Island, Nassau, expected 2025; Royal Beach Club Cozumel, 2026; Perfect Day Mexico, 2027; a Silversea hotel in Puerto Williams, Chile) and terminal interests (20% of the PortMiami terminal entity; iCON partnership terminals in Italy and Spain) are left out of sites.
